title: How to Make Money With Tariffs While Everyone Panics
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast

idea.name: Alternative manufacturer PDF
idea.one_liner: Sell US companies a PDF listing alternative manufacturers for products they already sell.
idea.customer: US companies already selling the products
idea.offer: A PDF of alternative manufacturers
idea.revenue_model: Sell the PDF; price not stated

key_quotes.quote: Can you sell it in a PDF to companies here in the US that are already selling those products?

ideas.delivery: Provide the manufacturer information in a PDF; the speaker does not describe who prepares or delivers it.

idea.name: Tariff-affected supplier sourcing agent
idea.one_liner: Find alternative manufacturers for US importers and earn a broker, finder or contingent fee when they use one.
idea.customer: American companies importing from tariff-affected countries, including Shopify stores
idea.offer: Research and source alternative manufacturers for client products
idea.revenue_model: A percentage of imports as a broker or finder fee, or a fee charged only if the client uses a supplier; exact rate not stated

key_quotes.quote: you can act as a sourcing agent for them and make a percentage of everything they import as a broker's fee or a finder fee.
Tell me three products of yours that you'd like a better manufacturer for, and I'll find you alternatives, and I'll only charge you if I find someone that you end up using.

claims.claim: The offer promises to find alternative factories within 24 hours.
claims.quote: I'll find you better factories within 24 hours.

claims.claim: The offer asks a client to name three products for sourcing research.
claims.quote: Tell me three products of yours that you'd like a better manufacturer for

claims.claim: A virtual assistant list of Shopify stores is said to cost 20 to 50 bucks on Upwork.
claims.quote: Or you could go to Upwork and do the same thing for 20 to 50 bucks.

claims.claim: The speaker says new-product arrival lead time can be one to three months.
claims.quote: Another thing about import Yeti is you can have a 1 to 3 month lead time on new products

claims.claim: The outreach script identifies a store's three best-selling products.
claims.quote: So, when you reach out cold to these Shopify stores, just tell them that you know what their three bestselling products are.

claims.claim: The speaker estimates that over 95% of people will not respond to the outreach.
claims.quote: 95 plus% of people will never respond no matter how good your offer or email is.

acquisition_channels.details: Email Shopify stores with a tailored offer and examples of their best-selling products.

ideas.delivery: Research alternative manufacturers and introduce them to the client; the speaker also suggests comparing product samples.

prices: 20 to 50 bucks for a virtual assistant list

uk_legal_risk.reason: The strategy relies on cold email to store owners or executives without limiting recipients to limited companies; UK cold email to sole traders is prohibited, and corporate emails need an opt-out.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to personal contact data used for prospecting.

idea.name: Offshore staffing agency
idea.one_liner: Hire and manage offshore virtual assistants for companies, charging clients a markup on worker pay.
idea.customer: Companies that want offshore staff
idea.offer: Recruit, manage and supply remote workers, handling hiring and firing
idea.revenue_model: Mark up hourly pay by 50–100%; speaker describes a 50% margin

key_quotes.quote: You mark up their seven or $8 an hour by 50 to 100%.
You manage them. You deal with the headaches of hiring, firing, and you take a 50% margin right off the top.

claims.claim: The suggested worker pay is seven or eight dollars an hour, marked up by 50 to 100%.
claims.quote: You mark up their seven or $8 an hour by 50 to 100%.

claims.claim: The speaker says the staffing agency could take a 50% margin.
claims.quote: You deal with the headaches of hiring, firing, and you take a 50% margin right off the top.

ideas.delivery: The agency hires and manages offshore workers and handles hiring and firing for client placements.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK-based staffing or employment businesses may be subject to the Employment Agencies Act 1973 and Conduct of Employment Agencies and Employment Businesses Regulations 2003.

idea.name: Offshore placement agency

key_quotes.quote: Number two, placement agency, where you charge a flat fee or a percentage of the first year's salary in exchange for finding and placing a competent overseas employee.

claims.claim: The suggested one-time placement fee is $500 to $5,000.
claims.quote: You go to Upwork, you find some rockstar virtual assistants, and you place them at companies for a onetime placement fee, $500 to $5,000.

claims.claim: The suggested alternative fee is 10 to 30% of first-year salary.
claims.quote: You can do a flat fee, or you can do 10 to 30% of their first year salary.

ideas.delivery: Find candidates, vet them and place them with a company; the speaker does not specify ongoing management.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK-based recruitment or placement agencies may be subject to the Employment Agencies Act 1973 and Conduct of Employment Agencies and Employment Businesses Regulations 2003.

idea.name: Affordable domestically made e-commerce
idea.one_liner: Sell affordable, high-quality goods manufactured domestically, emphasizing their US-made origin.
idea.customer: Consumers willing to buy domestically made products at an affordable price
idea.offer: E-commerce goods made domestically, potentially handmade
idea.revenue_model: Retail product sales; price not stated

key_quotes.quote: That's probably the best type of e-commerce business you could start right now.
Kind of like corn chips that say gluten-free. Yeah, there's no gluten in corn. They're naturally gluten-free. But who cares if it gets 5% of more people to buy your chips?

claims.claim: The speaker says US consumers are only really willing to buy US-made products if they are affordable enough.
claims.quote: I don't know if you've noticed, but Americans are only really willing to buy made in America products if they're affordable enough.

claims.claim: The speaker suggests emphasizing a product attribute could get 5% more people to buy chips.
claims.quote: But who cares if it gets 5% of more people to buy your chips?

ideas.delivery: Sell domestically manufactured goods through an e-commerce store; the speaker suggests highlighting their origin in the branding.
